title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 29 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 29)

content.overview: Section 29 provides that, unless the parties agree otherwise, decisions of a multi-member tribunal are made by majority. Procedural questions may be decided by the presiding arbitrator where authorised by the parties or all tribunal members.
content.glance: Section 29 provides that, unless the parties agree otherwise, decisions of a multi-member tribunal are made by majority. Procedural questions may be decided by the presiding arbitrator where authorised by the parties or all tribunal members.
content.study:
Section 29 — Decision making by panel of arbitrators

Section 29 provides that, unless the parties agree otherwise, decisions of a multi-member tribunal are made by majority. Procedural questions may be decided by the presiding arbitrator where authorised by the parties or all tribunal members.

Apply the provision by identifying operative conditions, exceptions, procedural stage and connected provisions. Do not substitute generic arbitration practice for the statutory rule.
